questions.q: Two metal spheres of radius $R$ and $3 R$ have same surface charge density $\sigma$. If they are brought in contact and then separated, the surface charge density on smaller and bigger sphere becomes $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$, respectively. The ratio $\frac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}$ is.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For conducting sphere, $\mathrm{V}=\frac{\sigma \mathrm{r}}{\varepsilon_0}$
After contact, $\mathrm{V}_1=\mathrm{V}_2$
$\begin{aligned}
& \sigma_1 r_1=\sigma_2 r_2 \\ & \frac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}=\frac{r_2}{\mathrm{r}_1} \\ & \frac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2}=3
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Charges ${Q}_{1}$ and~${Q}_{2}$ are at points~$A$ and~$B$~of a right-angled triangle~$OAB$. The resultant electric field at point~$O$ is perpendicular to the hypotenuse, then~${Q}_{1} / {Q}_{2}$ is proportional to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using triangle properties

$tan\text{\theta} = \dfrac{x1}{x2}tan\text{\theta} = \dfrac{E2}{E1} = \dfrac{K{Q}_{2} / {x}_{2}^{2}}{K{Q}_{1} / {x}_{1}^{2}} ⇒ \dfrac{x1}{x2} = \dfrac{K{Q}_{2} / {x}_{2}^{2}}{K{Q}_{1} / {x}_{1}^{2}}$

~$\dfrac{Q1}{Q2} =$~$\dfrac{x1}{x2}$

questions.q: An electric charge ${10}^{- 6}\muC$ is placed at origin $( 0, 0 )m$ of $X - Y$ co-ordinate system. Two points $P$ and $Q$ are situated at $( \sqrt{3}, \sqrt{3} ) m$ and $( \sqrt{6}, 0 ) m$ respectively. The potential difference between the points $P$ and $Q$ will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the potential difference between $P$ and $Q$ is given by

$∆ V = kq \left(\dfrac{1}{r1} - \dfrac{1}{r2}\right) . . .\left($1\right)$

Now,

\begin{cases}{r}_{1}$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\sqrt{( \sqrt{3}{)}^{2} + ( \sqrt{3}{)}^{2}}$m \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\sqrt{6}$m\end{cases}$

And,

\begin{cases}{r}_{2}$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\sqrt{( \sqrt{6}{)}^{2} + 0}$m \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\sqrt{6}$m\end{cases}$

As ${r}_{1} = {r}_{2} = $\sqrt{6}$m$ and the value of the charge remains constant, the potential difference between the points is zero.

$

questions.q: A dipole comprises of two charged particles of identical magnitude $q$ and opposite in nature. The~mass $m$~of the positive charged particle is half of the mass of the negative charged particle. The two charges are separated by a distance~$l$ . If the dipole is placed in a uniform electric field $\overset{→}{E}$; in such a way that dipole axis makes a very small angle with the electric field, $\overset{→}{E}$. The angular frequency of the oscillations of the dipole when released is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The data given is&

$l =$distance between the charges

$q =$charge

$m =$mass of the positive charge

$2m=$mass of negative charge~

The moment of inertia of the system is~

$I = \left(\dfrac{m \times 2m}{m + 2m}\right)\left(l\right)2 = \dfrac{2ml^{2}}{3}$

The angular frequency can be written as~

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{pE}{I}} . . . ( i )$

Substituting the value of moment of inertia in the equation (i) we get~

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{pE}{\dfrac{2ml^{2}}{3}}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3pE}{2ml^{2}}}$

The value of the dipole moment is

$p = ql$

Hence, the angular frequency becomes

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{3qE}{2ml}}$

This question was given bonus by NTA as none of the options matched in the original paper.

questions.q: A charge $q$~is placed at one corner of a cube as shown in figure. The flux of electrostatic field~$\overset{→}{E}$ through the shaded area is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
flux through cube $= \dfrac{q}{8{ϵ}_{0}}$

flux through surfaces $ABEH, ADGH, ABCD$~will be zero

$ϕ\left(EFGH\right) = ϕ \left(DCFG\right) = ϕ \left($EBCF\right) = $\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{q}{8{ϵ}_{0}}\right)

$= $\dfrac{q}{24{ϵ}_{0}}

$

questions.q: Two identical metallic spheres $A$ and $B$ when placed at certain distance in air repel each other with a force of $F$. Another identical uncharged sphere $C$ is first placed in contact with $A$ and then in contact with $B$ and finally placed at midpoint between spheres $A$and $B$. The force experienced by sphere $C$ will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let charge on& $A$~and~$B$~be~${q}_{A} = {q}_{B} = q$.

Then force acting between them is~$F = \dfrac{Kq^{2}}{r2}$.

When $C$ is placed in contact with $A$, charge on $A$~and~$C$ will be $= \dfrac{q}{2}$

Now $C$ is placed in contact with $B$, charge on $B$~ and~$C$ will be $= \dfrac{q + \dfrac{q}{2}}{2} = \dfrac{3q}{4}$

Now, force experienced by sphere~$C$~is~

$F^{'} = {F}_{2} - {F}_{1} = \dfrac{K9q^{2}}{16 \times \dfrac{r2}{4}} - \dfrac{K3q^{2}}{8 \times \dfrac{r2}{4}} = \left(K\dfrac{3q}{4} - K\dfrac{q}{2}\right)\dfrac{r2}{4} \times \dfrac{3q}{4}$

$= \dfrac{3Kq^{2}}{4r^{2}} = \dfrac{3F}{4}$

questions.q: Four point charges $- q, + q, + q$ and $- q$ are placed on y-axis at $y = - 2d, y = - d,$ and $y = + 2d,$ respectively. The magnitude of the electric field $E$ at a point on the x-axis at $x = D,$ with $D ≫ d,$ will behave as:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The electric field at $P$ is superposition of the fields due to all four charges. The electric field due to the two $+ q$ charges is

${E}_{+ q} = \dfrac{Kq}{D^{2} + d^{2}}{cos ⁡ \theta}_{1} \times 2$
${E}_{- q} = \dfrac{Kq}{D^{2} + 4d^{2}}{cos ⁡ \theta}_{2} \times 2$
The field due to $+ q$ is towards right and the field due to $- q$ is towards left. Also ${\theta}_{1} \approx 0$ and ${\theta}_{2} \approx 0$ .
$∴ {E}_{net} = {E}_{+ q} - {E}_{- q} \approx \dfrac{Kq}{D^{2} + d^{2}} - \dfrac{Kq}{D^{2} + 4d^{2}}$
$= \dfrac{Kq3d^{2}}{\left(D^{2} + d^{2}\right)\left(D^{2} + 4d^{2}\right)} \approx \dfrac{3Kqd^{2}}{D4}$
$E ∝ \dfrac{1}{D^{4}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Using } \Delta V=E(\Delta d) \\ & V=E(10) \\ & V_{A B}=E \cdot 4=\frac{V}{10} \times 4=\frac{2 V}{5}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In a cuboid of dimension $2L \times 2L \times L$ , a charge $q$ is placed at the centre of the surface $S$~having area of $4L^{2}$ . The flux through the opposite surface to $S$& is given by
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Assume& a similar cuboid on top of the given cuboid to make symmetry about charge. Thus, it becomes a cube of length& $2L$.

Flux~passing through whole cube is~$ϕ = \dfrac{q}{\in 0}$(Gauss's Law).

Since, total faces are $6$, so flux~passing through shaded face~$= \dfrac{q}{6{∈}_{0}}$.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Net dipole moment of a polar linear isotropic dielectric substance is not zero even in the absence of an external electric field.
Reason (R) : In absence of an external electric field, the different permanent dipoles of a polar dielectric substance are oriented in random directions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: (A) is correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not correct
Both $(\mathrm{A})$ and $(\mathrm{R})$ are correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but $(\mathrm{R})$ is correct
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A : Since polar dielectrics are randomly oriental $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}}_{\mathrm{net}}=\overrightarrow{0}$.
R : If $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}$ is absent, polar dielectric remain polar \& are randomly oriented.

questions.q: A vertical electric field of magnitude $4 . 9 \times {10}^{5}NC^{- 1}$ just prevents a water droplet of a mass $0 . 1g$ from falling. The value of charge on the droplet will be : (Given $g = 9 . 8ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
To balance gravitational force, electric force on the liquid drop should act in upward direction.

For translational equilibrium along vertical direction,

$qE = mg$

$⇒ q = \dfrac{mg}{E} = \dfrac{0 . 1 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 9 . 8}{4 . 9 \times {10}^{5}} = 2 . 0 \times {10}^{- 9}C$

questions.q: Four equal point charges $Q$ each are placed in the $xy$ plane at \left(0, 2\right),  \left(4, 2\right), \left($4, - 2\right)$ and  \left(0, - 2\right)$ . The work required to put a fifth charge $Q$ at the origin of the coordinate system will be:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work done in bringing the fifth charge at origin is equal to change in the potential energy of the system of charges.

${W}_{ext} = \Delta U= {U}_{f} - {U}_{i}$ if ${U}_{i} = 0$ (assumed)

${W}_{ext} = {U}_{f} - 0= \left[\dfrac{KQ^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{KQ^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{KQ^{2}}{2\sqrt{5}} + \dfrac{KQ^{2}}{2\sqrt{5}}\right]

Hence, the work done in bringing the fifth charge at the origin is~
${W}_{ext} = $\dfrac{Q^{2}}{4\pi{ε}_{0}} \left[$1 + $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right].

$

questions.q: If two charges ${q}_{1}$and~${q}_{2}$~are separated with distance $d$~and placed in a medium of dielectric constant $k$. What will be the equivalent distance between charges in air for the same electrostatic force?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The force between the two charges when they are placed in& dielectric is

${F}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{o}k}\dfrac{{q}_{1}{q}_{2}}{d2}$

The force~between the two charges~when they are placed at separation~$d '$~is

${F}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{o}}\dfrac{{q}_{1}{q}_{2}}{d{'}^{2}}$

Since, the force between the two charges is same in both case

${F}_{1} = {F}_{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{o}k}\dfrac{{q}_{1}{q}_{2}}{d2} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi{ε}_{o}}\dfrac{{q}_{1}{q}_{2}}{d{'}^{2}}$

$⇒ d ' = d\sqrt{k}$

questions.q: A dipole with two electric charges of $2 \mu \mathrm{C}$ magnitude each, with separation distance $0.5 \mu \mathrm{~m}$, is placed between the plates of a capacitor such that its axis is parallel to an electric field established between the plates when a potential difference of 5 V is applied. Separation between the plates is 0.5 mm. If the dipole is rotated by $30^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ from the axis, it tends to realign in the direction due to a torque. The value of torque is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{E}=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{\mathrm{~d}}=\frac{5}{5 \times 10^{-4}}=10^4 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{m} \\ & \tau=\mathrm{PE} \sin \theta
\end{aligned}$
Where $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{qa}=2 \times 10^{-6} \times 5 \times 10^{-7}$
$=1 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{m}$
$\tau=1 \times 10^{-12} \times 10^4 \times \frac{1}{2}=5 \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{~N}-\mathrm{m}$

questions.q: An infinitely long positively charged straight thread has a linear charge density $\lambda \mathrm{Cm}^{-1}$. An electron revolves along a circular path having axis along the length of the wire. The graph that correctly represents the variation of the kinetic energy of electron as a function of radius of circular path from the wire is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Electric field $\mathrm{E}$ at a distance $\mathrm{r}$ due to infinite long wire is $E=\frac{2 k \lambda}{r}$ Force of electron $\Rightarrow F=e E\begin{aligned} & F=e\left(\frac{2 k \lambda}{r}\right) \\ & F=\frac{2 k \lambda e}{r} \end{aligned}$
This force will provide required centripetal force $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{F} & =\frac{\mathrm{m}^2}{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{r}} \\ \mathrm{v} & =\sqrt{\frac{2 \mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}}} \\ \mathrm{KE} & =\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~m}\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e}}{\mathrm{m}}\right) \\ & =\mathrm{k} \lambda \mathrm{e} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: Consider two charged metallic spheres ${S}_{1}$ and ${S}_{2}$ of radii ${R}_{1}$ and ${R}_{2},$ respectively. The electric fields ${E}_{1}$ (on ${S}_{1}$ ) and ${E}_{2}$ (on ${S}_{2}$ ) on their surfaces are such that $\dfrac{{E}_{1}}{{E}_{2}} = \dfrac{{R}_{1}}{{R}_{2}} .$ Then the ratio ${V}_{1}$ (on ${S}_{1}$ )$/{V}_{2}$ (on ${S}_{2}$ ) of the electrostatic potentials on each sphere is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,& $\dfrac{E1}{E2} = \dfrac{R1}{R2}$
Then ratio of potential would be,$\dfrac{V1}{V2} = \dfrac{{E}_{1}{R}_{1}}{{E}_{2}{R}_{2}} = \dfrac{R1}{R2} \times \dfrac{R1}{R2} = \left(\dfrac{R1}{R2}\right)2$

questions.q: A small uncharged conducting sphere is placed in contact with an identical sphere but having $4 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{C}$ charge and then removed to a distance such that the force of repulsion between them is $9 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~N}$. The distance between them is (Take $\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_{\mathrm{o}}}$ as $9 \times 10^9 \mathrm{in} \mathrm{SI}$ units)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{F}=\frac{\mathrm{k}\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right)}{\mathrm{r}^2} \\ & 9 \times 10^{-3}=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times\left(4 \times 10^{-8}\right) \times 4 \times 10^{-8}}{4 \times \mathrm{r}^2} \\ & \mathrm{r}^2=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 16 \times 10^{-16}}{4 \times 9 \times 10^{-3}}=4 \times 10^{-4} \\ & \mathrm{r}=2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m} \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An electric dipole is placed on $x -$axis in proximity to a line charge of linear charge density $3 . 0 \times {10}^{- 6}Cm^{- 1} .$~Line charge is placed on $z -$axis and positive and negative charge of dipole is at a distance of $10$ mm and $12$ mm from the origin respectively. If total force of $4N$ is exerted on the dipole, find out the amount of positive or negative charge of the dipole.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$r = 10mm, x = 2,$
\left|\overset{→}{F}q\right| = \dfrac{2k\lambda}{r} \cdot q$
\left|\overset{→}{F}- q\right| = \dfrac{2k\lambda}{r + x} \cdot q$

\left|\overset{→}{F}net\right| = \dfrac{2k\lambdaq \cdot x}{r ( r + x )}$
$4 = \dfrac{2 \times 9 \times {10}^{9} \times 3 \times {10}^{- 6} \times q \times 2mm}{10mm . 12mm}$

$⇒ q = 4 . 44\muC$

$

questions.q: An electric field is given by $( 6\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} ) NC^{- 1}$. The electric flux through a surface area $30\overset{^}{i}m^{2}$ lying in YZ-plane(in SI unit) is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

$\overset{→}{E} = ( 6\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} ) NC^{- 1}$

$\overset{→}{A} = 30\overset{^}{i}m^{2}$

$ϕ = \overset{→}{E} \cdot \overset{→}{A}$

$⇒ ϕ = ( 6\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k} ) \cdot ( 30\overset{^}{i} ) = 180\text{SI unit}$

questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: An electric dipole of dipole moment is $6 . 0 \times {10}^{- 6}Cm$ placed in a uniform electric field of $1 . 5 \times {10}^{3}NC^{- 1}$ in such a way that dipole moment is along electric field. The work done in rotating dipole by $180 °$in this field will be_______mJ.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The work done for rotating a dipole is given by the change in the potential energy. The potential energy is given by

$U = - \overset{→}{p} \cdot \overset{→}{E}$

$W = ∆ U = {U}_{f} - {U}_{i}$

So, the work done is~

~$W = - pEcos180 ° - ( - pEcos0 ° ) = 2pE = 2 \times 6 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 1 . 5 \times {10}^{3} = 18mJ$

questions.q:
An electric field $\overset{→}{E} = 4x\overset{^}{i} - \left(y^{2} + 1\right)\overset{^}{j}N / C$ passes through the box shown in figure. The flux of the electric field through surfaces $ABCD$ and $BCGF$ are marked as ${ϕ}_{\text{I}}$ and ${ϕ}_{\text{II}}$ respectively. The difference between \left({ϕ}_{I} - {ϕ}_{II}\right)$ is (in $Nm^{2} / C$ ) ____________.

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Flux via $ABCD$
${ϕ}_{1} = ∫ E . dA = 0$
Flux via $BCEF$
${ϕ}_{2} = ∫ E . dA$
${ϕ}_{2} = E . A = \left(4x\overset{^}{i} - \left(y^{2} + 1\right)\overset{^}{j}\right) . 4\overset{^}{i}$
$= 16xwhere, x = 3$
${ϕ}_{2} = 48\dfrac{N . m^{2}}{C}{ϕ}_{1} - {ϕ}_{2} = - 48\dfrac{N . m^{2}}{C}$

questions.q:
A $1m$ long copper wire carries a current of $1A$. If the cross section of the wire is $2 . 0{mm}^{2}$ and the resistivity of copper is $1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8}Ωm$. The force experienced by moving electron in the wire is _____\times {10}^{- 23}N$

(Charge of electron$= 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}C )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, length& $l = 1m$, current~$i = 1A$, area $A = 2 \times {10}^{- 6}m$~and resistivity~$ρ = 1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8}Ωm$.

Resistance of wire is~$R = \dfrac{ρl}{A} = \dfrac{1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 8} \times 1}{2 \times {10}^{- 5}} = \dfrac{1 . 7}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}Ω$

Now, electric field in the wire is~$E = ρJ$, where,~$J = \dfrac{i}{A}$~is current density.

Thus,~$E = \dfrac{iρ}{A} = iR = 1 \times \dfrac{1 . 7}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}Vm^{- 1}$

Electric force in terms of electric field is given by~$F = qE$

Therefore, force experienced by moving electron is $F = 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times \dfrac{1 . 7}{2} \times {10}^{- 2}$

$= 1 . 36 \times {10}^{- 21}= 136 \times {10}^{- 23}N$

questions.q: At the centre of a half ring of radius $\mathrm{R}=10 \mathrm{~cm}$ and linear charge density $4 \mathrm{n} \mathrm{C} \mathrmm^{-1}$, the potential is $x \pi \mathrm{V}$. The value of $x$ is _______
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Potential at centre of half ring
$\begin{aligned} & V=\frac{K Q}{R} \\ & V=\frac{K \lambda \pi R}{R} \\ & V=K \lambda \pi \Rightarrow V=9 \times 10^9 \times 4 \times 10^{-9} \pi \\ & V=36 \pi\end{aligned}$
